# Selective Ambition: The Joy of Missing Out on Purpose

> A book by Gaurav Srivastava. The case for caring deeply about fewer things, and letting the rest go on purpose: the Joy of Missing Out (JOMO) reframed as a deliberate way of choosing, working, and living amid infinite options and AI-era pressure.

Selective Ambition argues that the modern problem is not poor time management but too many open doors. It is not a productivity system; it is a case for intentional subtraction, grounded in named research on attention, comparison, and choice, and in the author's own experience of AI-era abundance and burnout. Full and fulfilling, the book argues, are two different things.

## The book
- Title: Selective Ambition: The Joy of Missing Out on Purpose
- Author: Gaurav Srivastava (close to two decades in technology; built and sold a consultancy; now works hands-on with AI)
- Buy: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HDKFJTF3 (Kindle, ASIN B0HDKFJTF3, published 2026-08-09, English)

## Core ideas
- Full and fulfilling are two different things.
- Busy vs stretched: only one can be fixed with a calendar.
- The intentional "no": hard, soft, and structural.
- One-thing seasons: choose depth over forced breadth.
- The 5% shift: JOMO for people who cannot simply walk away.

## Research the book cites
- The Paradox of Choice (Barry Schwartz) and the Iyengar & Lepper jam study
- Social Comparison Theory (Leon Festinger, 1954)
- Hedonic adaptation / the hedonic treadmill (Brickman & Campbell)
- The social pain of rejection (Naomi Eisenberger, 2003, fMRI)
- Flow (Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi); burnout as loss of agency (Maslach & Leiter)
